correctness.rationale: The conditional PGF solves the exact forward birth–death–immigration equation; the stationary age density follows from finite-mean renewal theory. Subcritical local masses are obtained by an explicit uniform three-window ratio argument and asymptotics for Gamma(n+k)/n!. The critical product of Lomax age and independent Gamma intensity is regularly varying with the precise Gamma-moment coefficient; conditional Poisson Chernoff estimates preserve the tail. For supercritical birth dominance, exponentially growing conditional intensity turns the equilibrium-age tail into an exact logarithmic tail with coefficient; Gamma extremes and Poisson fluctuation errors are negligible. Subcritical finite moments, the critical sharp power cutoff and supercritical divergence follow from the proven tails. 53 numerical differential-equation and quadrature checks were run from the actual standalone verify.py file, but do not prove the asymptotic limits.

value.rationale: The previously studied zero-range birth–death–immigration marginal becomes qualitatively different under a natural nonmemoryless complete-reset protocol: finite stationary mass exists in all three phases but the exact occupation tail changes from exponential-with-log suppression, through polynomial with a Gamma prefactor, to a logarithmic tail with no positive moments. This distinguishes stationarity from moment stabilization and gives closed, mathematically motivated diagnostics for population catastrophes. The result is a parameter-uniform exact classification, not a finite numerical table, trivial rescaling or claim about solving the coupled lattice.
